fatal_errors: The proposed initially homogeneous single-phase alloy does not match the as-cast FCC+B2 AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic alloy.

The hypothesis attributes embrittlement to grain-boundary precipitation and intergranular cracking, whereas the target mechanism is enhanced L12 ordering, planar slip, and plastic instability at jagged FCC/B2 phase-boundary tips without impurity segregation.
It omits the defining non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile response, including maximum embrittlement near 600°C and recovery near 750°C.
The cited studies concern different HEAs and demonstrate phase decomposition or precipitation but do not establish toughness loss, crack initiation, or the proposed grain-boundary mechanism.
explanation: The response addresses thermally induced toughness degradation and offers a falsifiable treated-versus-control experiment, but it largely restates the conventional grain-boundary precipitation expectation that the requested comparison was meant to distinguish. Temperatures, aging windows, L12 ordering, APBE/modulus effects, restricted cross-slip, jagged FCC/B2 boundaries, and ductile transition zones are all absent. Its generic high-temperature-plus-cyclic-loading intervention also confounds thermal and mechanical effects and supplies no composition-specific service window. E1 supports nanoscale B2/BCC decomposition in another alloy, and E2 reports boundary precipitation after powder processing and sintering in a refractory HEA; neither supports intergranular embrittlement or reduced fracture toughness. Thus the proposal is testable in a broad sense but neither reconstructs the target nor has sufficient direct evidence to qualify as a well-supported alternative.
